page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Parasitism is an interaction between two
organisms of different species in which one
is benefited and the other is harmed.
The one that gains is the parasite; the one
that is harmed is the host.
steps.why: Naming the two partners in the definition itself saves a sentence later and shows the examiner that the words parasite and host are being used correctly.
common_mistakes: Writing that the other partner is unaffected. That is commensalism.
Calling the host the parasite. The host is the one that is harmed.
steps.memory_tip: Count the gains again: mutualism two, commensalism one and a zero, parasitism one and a minus.
steps.margin_note: One sentence, then one line naming the parasite and the host.

steps.label: Example

lines.text: The parasite gains, the host is harmed

lines: Ex: Plasmodium vivax, the malarial parasite,
The parasite gets food and shelter from the
The man gets malaria, so he is harmed.
steps.why: The example must show the harm as well as the gain, because the harm is the one thing that separates parasitism from the other two interactions.
common_mistakes: Naming the parasite without saying what harm it does. The harm carries the mark.
Giving a lion and a deer. The lion kills the deer outright, so that is predation.
steps.memory_tip: Plasmodium in man: food and shelter for the parasite, malaria for the host.
steps.margin_note: Name the parasite and the host, then one line of gain and one of harm.

insider_note: Parasitism, predation, commensalism and mutualism are marked as a set — always write what happens to BOTH partners.
